sections.content:
Population change in Great Yarmouth in 2032

The population in Great Yarmouth is projected to increase from 99,834 people in 2022 to 102,382 people in 2032.

Despite an overall increase in the population, there is projected to be a fall in births and deaths, which will decrease the population by 5,065 people.

This is different to the majority of areas in England, where net internal migration is projected to be the biggest factor in population change.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Great Yarmouth
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In Great Yarmouth, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More deaths than births mean that the population is projected to decrease by 5,065, with 8,300 births and 13,365 deaths in Great Yarmouth between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would decrease the population in Great Yarmouth by 5.1%, compared with an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to increase the population by 4,760, with 51,401 people moving to the area and 46,641 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Great Yarmouth by 4.8%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to reduce the population by 223, with 986 people moving to the area and 1,209 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Great Yarmouth by 0.2%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 3,056, with 6,776 people moving to the area and 3,720 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Great Yarmouth by 3.1%, compared with an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in Great Yarmouth in 2032

The median age in Great Yarmouth is projected to rise from 46 years in 2022 to 48 years in 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 27% of the population in Great Yarmouth are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 23% in 2022.

sections.title: The 50 to 59 age group are set to see the largest change in Great Yarmouth between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Great Yarmouth is projected to stay the same, at around 59%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to rise from 386 to 412 over the same time period.

This is above average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Great Yarmouth?

In 2032, 18% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 20% in 2022.

This is below average for England in 2032 (20%).

Looking at the youngest age groups in Great Yarmouth between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will fall from 5% to 4%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 8% to 6%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will fall from 8% to 7%
